Daily Bitbucket user: browsing source code via the web is quite painful. Quickly looking at someone's repository takes a lot of clicking and is way too slow compared to GitHub's slicker UI.
After importing some repos into Bitbucket: 'you really get what you pay for.' GitHub completely trounces Bitbucket on ease of use and toolset.
None of my existing Bitbucket repos have a Git link, and I can't find a way to add Git support from the Admin screen. Git is only an option when creating a new repo.
Cancelling a $7 GitHub plan and paying Bitbucket $10/month despite using only 2 users. Prefers paying per user rather than per repo for many small private repos.
The redesigned commits view is '100 times better than Github's ever was': much more info, plus a graph like gitx.
Redesign drawback: the readme is now narrow and can't expand, so <pre> text shows scrollbars, and headings have little whitespace, which looks cramped.
There is no way to browse or search projects hosted on Bitbucket, for example by language. The main page only shows screenshots and signup links. Wants an 'Explore' feature like GitHub's.

Chose self-hosted GitLab over Bitbucket or GitHub because it already has most of these features and allows multiple private repos on a cheap VPS. Sees no innovation in the redesign that puts Bitbucket ahead.
Likes the 'Approve' button on commits for peer review, something GitHub lacks.
Their support is great: they bailed us out of a nasty mess we got tangled up in with our repo.
Recently started using Bitbucket and likes it, but finds the team concept difficult and unintuitive. SVN support seems gone, so old repos must be re-imported as Git.
I use Bitbucket at work. And it stinks compared to Github.
We saved hundreds of dollars a month moving over to BitBucket last year.
Bitbucket's deploy keys fit typical use better than GitHub's: they are read-only and one key can be attached to multiple repos. GitHub's keys are read-write and limited to a single repo.
Likes Bitbucket's issue management much more than GitHub's. Hosting on Bitbucket plus free HipChat for small teams makes managing projects entirely through Atlassian fantastic.
Has used Bitbucket with Mercurial since 2011 and has 50+ hg repos to move manually. Disappointed; Bitbucket must provide a single-click way to convert a repo to Git.
A disaster for me: I've got dozens of hg repos on Bitbucket. Without automated conversion, there's probably no reason to keep using Bitbucket.
Shocked that all Mercurial repos will be deleted on June 1, 2020 rather than archived read-only like Google Code and CodePlex did. Historically interesting repos will disappear.

Admin of Bitbucket enterprise cloud says there appears to be no way to prevent team members from making repositories public. With sensitive data at stake, may switch to on-prem or GitHub Enterprise Cloud for better permissions.
A user leaving Bitbucket wants to preserve pull requests and comment threads, and is considering saving static HTML of the pages and rewriting links to point at migrated issues and hosted PR pages.
